data.narrative:
Credo Semiconductor is a publicly traded company in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, having completed its IPO in 2022. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable set of 3 public-stage peers in the same sector: Cerebras ($39.2B), Ouster ($2.3B), and Aeva Technologies ($1.1B).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach given available data. This method anchors valuation to the median valuation of the 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables, yielding $2.3B. The peer set exhibits substantial dispersion—the range spans $1.1B to $39.2B—reflecting heterogeneity in business models, scale, and market positioning within frontier semiconductor development. A public-comp anchoring approach using price-to-sales multiples (median 18.4x across ALAB, NVDA, and AMD) cannot be applied because Credo's revenue is not on file.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.9B to $2.6B, with a median point of $2.3B derived from the peer-median method. This represents the single quantitative anchor available. The primary uncertainty stems from limited methodological coverage—only one triangulation method is applicable—combined with the wide dispersion observed in the peer comparables, which suggests material differences in development stage, addressable market, or technical risk among semiconductor frontier companies. Revenue disclosure would enable multiples-based cross-validation.
